fields.h1: Build an Acupuncture Intake Form Read Before the First Needle
fields.hero_description: Build an acupuncture intake form that records each patient's pain, sleep, and digestion in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What the Practitioner Reads Before Needling
fields.features_subheading: An acupuncture intake form built in Emergent collects the answers that shape the first treatment plan.
fields.feature_1:
Questions on sleep, digestion, and heat

Ask how the patient sleeps, how meals sit afterward, and whether they tend to feel hot or cold. Each answer gets its own field, so the pattern is readable at a glance.
fields.feature_2:
A body map for where it hurts

Patients tap each sore spot on a front and back figure and score it from 0 to 10. The marks appear on the practitioner's chart beside the main complaint they typed in.
fields.feature_3:
A chart label when e-stim is ruled out

A yes to the pacemaker question puts a No e-stim label at the top of the patient's chart. The practitioner sees it while planning the first treatment, not halfway through.
fields.feature_4:
Medications and supplements, one per row

Patients list each medicine and supplement, herbs included, on its own row with the dose. The practitioner reads a clean list instead of a paragraph typed in a hurry at the door.
fields.feature_5:
Consent signed before the first needle

End with the clinic's consent statement and ask for a typed or drawn signature. The signature is stored with its date and the intake it belongs to, in a database you own.
fields.feature_6:
Source code a developer can take over

Export the code for the form and its chart screens to your GitHub repository on paid plans. A developer can host it on your own servers or keep building on it from there.

fields.usecase_heading: How Four Clinics Use the Answers
fields.tab_content_1:
Six out of 10 for back pain, logged from the tablet

Dovetail Community Acupuncture seats new patients in a shared room of recliners, and each one fills the intake on a tablet by the door. Aurelio Kestner marks low back pain and scores it 6 out of 10. He takes Recliner 4, and Wenqi Lattimore sees his complaint and score on her list before she walks over.
fields.tab_content_2:
No e-stim for any patient who has a pacemaker

Every new patient at Tarrowby Acupuncture answers a pacemaker question, because the clinic uses electroacupuncture for knee and back pain. Efua Asamoah answers yes before her 10:30 visit. Her chart opens with a No e-stim label, and Ruairi Bale plans a manual-needle treatment for her knee.
fields.tab_content_3:
Two medications and three supplements, one row each

Sebastian Pruett takes 2 prescription medications and 3 supplements, and the Stillbrook Herbs and Acupuncture intake gives each one a separate row and a dose field. Yumiko Lisle reads all 5 rows before she writes his herbal formula. Any row she wants to ask about gets a note for his first visit.
fields.tab_content_4:
Four neck pain scores line up into one chart

Leopold Strand answers one question each time he checks in at Kittering Acupuncture: how much his neck hurts today, from 0 to 10. He scored 7 at visit 1 and 3 at visit 4. Before visit 5, Thessaly Haldane opens his chart and sees all four scores as bars.

fields.howto_title: How to Create an Acupuncture Intake Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create an acupuncture intake form that puts the answers a treatment depends on in front of the practitioner.
fields.howto_step_1_des: List every answer that would change what happens in the first session: the main complaint, a pacemaker, pregnancy, current medications, and how the patient sleeps and digests. A question whose answer changes nothing about the treatment can come off the form.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Open with the main complaint and a 0 to 10 pain score, right after contact details. Add a body map with front and back views. A patient taps the sore spot instead of describing it in a text box.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Ask about sleep, digestion, appetite, and whether the patient runs hot or cold, in everyday words. Offer checkboxes such as wakes at night or bloating after meals, and leave one open field for anything the list misses.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Collect every prescription and supplement, herbs included, as a separate entry with its dose and how often it is taken. Ask about a pacemaker as a standalone yes or no question, which lets that one answer set a label on the chart.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Describe the clinic in one prompt
fields.howto_step_5_des: Put the questions and the chart labels into one prompt, along with who should see each answer. Emergent builds the acupuncture intake form, the patient database behind it, and a chart screen for practitioners. Ask for changes in plain English later.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Close the form with your consent statement and cancellation terms, followed by a typed or drawn signature. Keep the wording short enough to read on a phone, and keep a copy of each version so you know which one a patient signed.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Test it as a new patient
fields.howto_step_7_des: Fill in the form on a phone as a made-up patient with a pacemaker and two supplements. Check that the No e-stim label shows on the chart, that both supplements arrive as separate entries, and that the pain score lands in the database.

faq_plan.q: What is an acupuncture intake form?
faq_plan.a: An acupuncture intake form is the questionnaire a new patient fills out before the first acupuncture treatment. It covers contact details, the main complaint, health history, and medications. Acupuncture versions add Traditional Chinese Medicine questions about temperature, digestion, sleep, and emotional health, and the form ends with signed consent.

faq_plan.q: How do I create an acupuncture intake form?
faq_plan.a: List the questions that change a treatment, the labels the chart should show, and who reads each answer. Describe all of it in one prompt to Emergent's AI form builder. It builds the form and the database that stores every response, and any question can be changed later with another prompt.

faq_plan.q: What questions should an acupuncture intake form ask?
faq_plan.a: Start with the main complaint, where it hurts, and a pain score out of 10. Add health history, every medication and supplement, and a pacemaker question. Then come the pattern questions on sleep, appetite, digestion, and feeling hot or cold. Close with consent and a signature.

faq_plan.q: Can I reuse questions from another intake form for acupuncture?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Contact details and the medication list carry over from a dental intake form or any other health intake with few changes. What you add for acupuncture are the needle-specific questions, such as a pacemaker or a fear of needles, plus the pattern questions on sleep and digestion.

faq_plan.q: Can patients fill out an acupuncture intake form on their phone before the visit?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Send the link with the booking confirmation and the patient answers at home. The answers reach the chart before the visit, and a new patient who skipped it can finish on a tablet at the front desk. A form built with Emergent has no response caps.

faq_plan.q: How do I flag a pacemaker on an acupuncture intake form?
faq_plan.a: Ask it as a yes or no question of its own, and have a yes add a warning to the patient's chart. Patient guidance from the University of Edinburgh says electroacupuncture is not recommended for people with a pacemaker. Make that warning the first thing the practitioner reads on the chart.

faq_plan.q: How do I track pain scores on an acupuncture intake form between visits?
faq_plan.a: Ask returning patients the same question at every check-in: pain today, out of 10. Save each score with the visit number and show the scores as a chart on the patient's record. If your clinic also offers physical therapy, use the same scale on the pt intake form and both records line up.

faq_plan.q: Should an acupuncture intake form ask about herbs and supplements?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Some supplements can decrease the effects of medicines, while others can increase their effects, according to the National Institutes of Health. List herbs and supplements next to the prescriptions, each with its dose, for the practitioner to review before writing any herbal formula.

faq_plan.q: Can I keep acupuncture intake form responses in my own database?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Data from an acupuncture intake form built with Emergent lives in a database you own, where each patient's visits and signed consent sit together. On paid plans you can also export the full code to your GitHub repository.

faq_plan.q: Should an acupuncture intake form ask about stress and mood?
faq_plan.a: Yes, briefly. One or two questions on stress and mood fit the emotional health part of the pattern questions. Keep it short: a full mental health history belongs on a therapy intake form, completed with a counselor.

plan.angle: The SERP is a wall of downloadable acupuncture intake PDFs from individual clinics and template galleries that print the same Traditional Chinese Medicine checklist (temperature, digestion, sleep, emotions) and stop there. This page explains which answers change the first treatment and shows four acupuncture practices whose online intake acts on them: a community clinic that seats new patients from a tablet, a pacemaker answer that rules out electroacupuncture on the chart, a herbal practice that gets every medication and supplement as its own row, and returning patients whose pain scores become a chart.
